submission.natural_language_explanation:
A broad head whose activity grows with how much text it has read: on the first ~8 tokens of plain prose it is silent (attention parked on the first token), but past ~40 tokens of running text of any kind it fires weakly to moderately (0.45-1.0) on scattered tokens while attending ~1.0 to one earlier content word, so any passage of three or more sentences or 40+ tokens is predicted active; even in short texts it fires (0.5-1.3) at the second member of a series - the 'and'/'or'/'nor'/'until'/'than' or comma right after a first conjunct noun ('the cats and dogs', 'between noon and midnight', 'iron, copper, zinc') - and on code, markup and JSON rows ('x = a + b; y = a - b;', '
  • One

Predicted inactive: plain prose of up to about 25 tokens (one or two simple sentences, short questions, headings) that has no comma, no 'and'/'or'/'nor'/'but', no 'than', no list, no code symbols and no repeated word; about 1 in 15 such texts crosses weakly at a stray word.

rival_explanations: A pure context-length head: activity depends only on how many tokens have been read, so short code lines, comma lists and 'the X and Y' objects are as silent as short plain prose, and any prose of 25+ tokens fires.

A narrow series/coordination head: it fires only at a connective or comma that starts the second member of a series, so long plain paragraphs without such connectives stay silent however much context precedes them.
An induction/copy head: it fires mainly on tokens that repeat an earlier token and copies what followed, so coordinated objects with no repeated word ('the cats and dogs') stay silent.
